summary: Reviewed 4 files (api-stores.ts, api.ts, api-stores.test.ts, api-store-conflicts.test.ts). All OWASP Top 10 categories assessed. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (defence-in-depth recommendation for WP-005 routing), 1 Low, 1 Info. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01/A03 — Defence-in-depth: When WP-005 wires the :storeId URL routes (PUT /api/stores/:storeId, DELETE /api/stores/:storeId, POST /api/stores/:storeId/default), the extracted storeId parameter should be validated with assertSafeSlug() or a SLUG_REGEX check before being passed to the handlers — consistent with how repoId/slugUrlParam are guarded in server.ts (lines 363-364). The handlers themselves are safe (storeId is used only for config lookup, never as a filesystem path), so the worst-case impact without this guard is a 404 response, but the validation guard is standard practice across all parameterized routes in this codebase.

A03 — runGit() uses execFile() (argument array, no shell) — confirmed no shell injection risk. storePath arrives from expandStorePath(entry.path) → path.resolve(), which normalises but does not contain the path. Acceptable for local-tool threat model; no containment guard is needed given the tool is a local developer utility with no remote access.

A05 — Error messages in api-stores.ts reflect the submitted/expanded path (e.g. 'Cannot create store directory: permission denied at ${expandedPath}'). Since the user submitted that path in the same request, there is no sensitive information leak. Acceptable for a local developer tool.

No security issues — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. A02 (crypto), A07 (auth/session), A08 (integrity), A09 (logging), A10 (SSRF) not applicable for this local-tool domain-split file. A06 confirmed clean: no new third-party dependencies introduced. A04 confirmed: Zod strict schemas block extra fields; body size limit (1 MiB MAX_BODY_BYTES) enforced by server.ts readBody(). CORS restricts origin to http://localhost:{port}.

comments.note: Fix-Forward — api-stores.ts UpdateStoreBodySchema: changed label from z.string().optional() to z.string(). Making the schema required removes the dead guard, eliminates the label! non-null assertion, and establishes the schema as the single source of truth for field requirements — consistent with how all other schemas in this file are defined.
